The Immigration Restriction Act of 1901 was Australia’s foundational legislation for the White Australia policy. The language dictation test (in a European language chosen by the officer) was deliberately designed to exclude non-white immigrants, especially Asians, while avoiding explicit racial wording to appear less discriminatory and to avoid diplomatic friction, particularly with Britain and allied nations.  

Option (A) is incorrect because the test was not about genuine educational standards — it was arbitrary and intended to be failed.  
Option (C) is wrong because the test did not assess useful expertise; manual laborers could be exempted if they had “special skill required by Australia” (see paragraph g), so expertise was separate from the language requirement.  
Option (D) is incorrect because the policy did not aim to bar all immigrants — it sought to restrict non-European immigrants while allowing British and other European immigration.  

Option (B) fits the historical context: the language test was a mechanism for racial exclusion without explicit race-based clauses.  

Final answer: (B)
